briefs.source_chain: Stronger US/Eurozone flash PMIs plus UN rhetoric (Iran deal further off, no Russia-sanctions consensus) drove bond yields sharply higher because the market had been underpricing terminal Fed funds, culminating in the 5Y yield breaking 5% for the first time since 2007 after a weak 3.20bp-tail auction, therefore raising Fed hike risk (market sees next hike in October; Barr says more hikes likely needed), while JPM still argues equities can grind higher because SPX earnings track nominal not real GDP, with bond vol (not yield level) the bigger risk, therefore JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral running +Tech vs -RTY, bullish only on lower oil/yields, bearish only on a consumer break or AI capex cut.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: PMIs + UN rhetoric to yields spiking (5Y breaks 5% post weak auction) to hike-risk repricing (Oct hike, Barr) to JPM's nominal-GDP equity-bull argument with bond-vol caveat to Brent/Iran rhetoric context to Tactically Cautious/Neutral +Tech vs -RTY stance with explicit bull/bear triggers.

briefs.source_chain: 10Y/5Y yields hit multi-year/2007-era highs alongside rising Brent and CPI, which looks like an inflation story but isn't, therefore (of ~97bps YTD nominal yield rise, only ~10bps is breakevens, which are stable, and term premium is range-bound) the move is about policy rates and a higher neutral rate, driven by economic strength, AI-capex-as-capital-competition, and geopolitics (Warsh), with Raskin's neutral-rate upper bound now being approached, and yesterday's strong PMIs/GDPNow/earnings growth adding fuel, possibly amplified by positioning.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures (97bps, 10bps breakevens, 18-month range-bound term premium, Warsh's three drivers with AI capex reading attributed to DB, Raskin's plausible-range/upper-bound framing, PMI/GDPNow 5.08%/~30% earnings growth as added fuel, positioning as possible amplifier).

briefs.source_chain: Strong US/Eurozone flash PMIs (58.4 vs 55.3; 53.1 vs 51.7) signaled resilient growth reinforcing the case for continued Fed hiking, and a Brent rebound (+3.86% to $103.08) on US-Iran deal doubts added hawkish pressure, therefore Fed October-hike odds rose 53%→69%→71% and ECB odds rose 48%→66%, with year-end Fed pricing at 37bps (near-even odds of two more hikes), driving the 10yr Treasury yield up 15.2bps to a post-2007 high of 5.11% (biggest one-day move since Liberation Day) and the 5yr above 5% for the first time since 2007, worsened by a weak $70bn 5yr auction tailing 3.1bps, with European yields at multi-year highs and the Franco-German spread at 110.4bps (highest since the 2012 euro crisis), therefore equities fell broadly (S&P -0.75%, biggest decline in a month) despite the strong growth data, with only energy gaining.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same figures throughout, in the same causal order.

briefs.source_chain: Agentic-AI anticipation/anxiety drove today's dispersion: big tech bid (Nasdaq record high) while banks were battered (Dow's worst loser, S&P flat), with Goldman flagging negative AI spillover into financials/insurance/subscription businesses compounding Fed-hike/flatter-curve pressure; oil swung repeatedly on Iran headlines (Hormuz-reopening report, Fars denial, Saudi pipeline hopes, Trump's 'very good meeting' comment vs. his no-deal-before-Midterms remark) ending with WTI down 3.5%, while Trump also pushed a diesel-export ban given Iran/Ukraine-driven price spikes; Treasury yields ended flat despite falling inflation expectations (Goldman's 'weird bit', real-rate demand staying high), hyperscaler credit widened a fourth day, and both LO and HF desks were net sellers despite subdued activity, with breadth (new lows over new highs for six sessions) echoing 1999/1929 per CNBC.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and sequence, same attributions (Goldman on AI spillover and the 'weird bit', CNBC on breadth), same figures (3.5% WTI, four days of wider hyperscaler credit, six sessions of new lows over new highs, 1999/1929).

distortions.what: Brief says Trump 'floated' a diesel export ban; source has him saying he already told his people to pursue it ('I've called for it within my people')
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — either phrasing signals the same policy risk to diesel/refiner exposure; the actionable takeaway (export-ban risk from Iran/Ukraine price spikes) is unchanged
